scenes.text: Have you ever wondered why the scent of fresh rain is so incredibly intoxicating to humans, especially since you are actually smelling a compound called geosmin released by microscopic soil bacteria?
Our minds are so insanely sensitive to this earthy aroma that your nose can easily detect geosmin at an unbelievable concentration of just five parts per trillion.
To put this super-ability in perspective, you are literally better at smelling wet dirt after a storm than a great white shark is at detecting a single drop of blood in an Olympic-sized pool.

Evolutionary scientists believe our ancient ancestors developed this tracking instinct to survive severe droughts, so comment below if you love this cozy smell, and follow me for more mind-blowing survival secrets!
